hints.text: Treat the digits as whole numbers first. Afterwards, think about how many decimal places the product should have.
$3 \times 4 = 12$. Each factor has one decimal place, so the product needs $1 + 1 = 2$ decimal places.
Writing $12$ with two decimal places gives $0.12$, so $0.3 \times 0.4 = 0.12$.

explanation: Multiply the digits as whole numbers: $3 \times 4 = 12$.
Count the decimal places: one in $0.3$ plus one in $0.4$ makes two in the product.
Move the point two places in from the right of $12$ and write a zero in front: $0.12$.
So $0.3 \times 0.4 = 0.12$, which is small because both factors are less than one half.

steps: $\frac{3}{10} \times \frac{4}{10} = \frac{12}{100} = 0.12$ ✓ — the hundredths explain the two decimal places.
